column4: Whoa, that's a huge cut!
I better call for help.
Hello, Brain.
Listen up.
We've got a serious cut section down here.
Blood is already gushing out.
I need you to send blood platelets and painkillers to come fix this ASAP.
Alright, the nerve's already told me.
Help is on the way.
Huh? What kind of medicine is this?
We're painkillers!
Oh, so you can talk?
Yeah, who doesn't?
Besides, I'm not even feeling pain.
Who assigned you to come here?
You are actually hilarious.
You really don't know what's going on in your own body.
The more we talk, the more the host feels pain.
Bro, stir it up.
Bro, how do we know which way the pain is?
There's only one way to find out.
We split up.
You go east, I'll go north.
Aha!
So you're the ones causing the pain.
Hey, I'm just doing my job.
Well, we're here to do ours.
Doc, how fast will this painkiller work?
My foot hurts so bad.
Painkillers don't heal the wound.
They simply block prostaglandins.
Those are the chemicals that send pain signals to your brain.
So the pain feels like it's gone.
Even though the medicine never actually searched for the injury,
it just turned the signal down.
Oh, that makes sense.
